name: Thinking Machines Lab
description: Thinking Machines Lab is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Thinking Machines Lab is a privately held artificial intelligence company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing with a disclosed valuation, a $2 billion seed round announced on July 15, 2025, valued the company at $12 billion.

Based in San Francisco, Thinking Machines Lab develops artificial intelligence models and offers Tinker, a service that customers use to train and customize their own models. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.

table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round. Nvidia did not disclose the amount of its March 2026 investment, which accompanied a multi-year computing partnership.
round_notes: In September 2026, The Information reported that Thinking Machines Lab was in talks to raise $5 billion to $6 billion at a pre-money valuation of at least $40 billion, with Accel expected to lead and Nvidia expected to provide about half. Thinking Machines Lab has not announced the round.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Andreessen Horowitz led the seed round, with participation from Nvidia, Accel, ServiceNow, Cisco, AMD and Jane Street. Nvidia made a further investment in March 2026 as part of its computing partnership with the company. Other investors include GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Conviction Partners.
spv_sentence: SEC filings show one special purpose vehicle formed to invest in Thinking Machines Lab, organized in 2025.
sources: Sources: Thinking Machines Lab's description of Tinker; reports by TechCrunch (July 15, 2025, March 10, 2026 and September 3, 2026) and CNBC (July 2025); reporting by The Information (September 2026); and SEC Form D filings.
